facts.name: Purple Coneflower
facts.notes: A long-blooming prairie classic, native to the central U.S. Leave the seed heads standing for goldfinches.

sources.title: Bordine's (Michigan garden center): perennials by bloom time, 2026
sources.note: Current perennial list from a Michigan garden center.

sources.title: Penn State Extension: Cutting Down Perennials in the Fall
sources.note: Cut peonies, daylilies, brunnera and speedwell in fall; cut bee balm and garden phlox with powdery mildew and destroy the leaves; rake up hosta leaves (slug eggs); cut yarrow and Shasta daisy flower stalks but keep the base leaves. Leave grasses, Siberian iris, baptisia, sedum, Joe-Pye weed, coneflower, black-eyed Susan and most natives standing; leave marginally hardy anise hyssop tops over winter; tidy hardy geraniums, heucheras, hellebores and moss phlox in spring.

companions.why: Combines well with purple coneflower, bee balm and native grasses; in gardens with Japanese anemones.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Anise Hyssop article

companions.why: Combines with yellow flowers such as coreopsis and goldenrod, pink ones such as purple coneflower, prairie grasses and silver plants such as Stachys (lamb's ear).

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Blazing Star article

companions.why: Combine with Penstemon 'Husker Red' or purple speedwells; works well with coreopsis, purple coneflower, blazing star, black-eyed Susan, little bluestem and prairie dropseed.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Butterfly Weed article

companions.why: Combines well with great blue lobelia, irises and marsh milkweed; also found with purple coneflower, blazing star and foxglove beardtongue.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Cardinal Flower article

companions.why: Pair with purple coneflower for an interplay of flower and foliage.
Walters Gardens (Zeeland, Michigan) lists varieties of these as companions: purple coneflower and Penstemon.

sources.title: Walters Gardens, Zeeland, Michigan: Garden Phlox companions

companions.why: Pair with dark-leaved Heuchera; combine with aster, tall sedums like 'Autumn Joy', yarrow, rudbeckias and purple coneflower.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Little Bluestem article

companions.why: A border is brightened when obedient plant is planted alongside goldenrods, little bluestem and purple coneflower.
Combined with fall-blooming sedums; a great filler between purple coneflower, liatris, black-eyed Susan and butterfly weed.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Prairie Dropseed article

companions.why: Combines well with ornamental grasses, anise hyssop, beebalm, daylilies, fall asters, liatris, purple coneflower and rudbeckias.
Izel Native Plants: plant wild strawberry intermingled with lanceleaf coreopsis and purple coneflower.
